Inclusive rows overlap; fractions must not be added and are not wall-clock percentages. Missing rows mean not reported, not zero. Profile/control ratios are perturbation diagnostics, not formal performance effect estimates.

RuntimeInner::publish_attempt::{closure#5} is the spawned attempt task, calling run_attempt then finish_attempt (conversation_runtime.rs:3647). It includes downstream work, not merely native client publication encoding. Its 180/410 and 254/530 live samples must not be described as the isolated publication cost.

Candidate FactSpool::disk_insert has 8/276, 13/284, 14/410 and 13/530 inclusive samples, but zero sampled intersections with sqlite3LockAndPrepare in these four records. That insertion already uses prepare_cached. This is evidence against treating the entire Source fact spool cost as a missing SQL-cache fix.

The directly observed uncached witness/completion/read SQL explains part of remaining prepare cost. No cache-hit/miss instrumentation was collected. These profiles do not establish that capacity 64 is thrashing or that raising it would help. The single profile/control pair per cell is noisy: observed profile/control mean turn time is 0.755-1.151x, CPU per turn 0.769-1.157x, whole lifecycle wall time 0.865-1.072x, lifecycle CPU 0.851-1.082x. Values below one demonstrate uncontrolled variation, not a negative causal profiling tax. Formal repeated unprofiled pairs must provide performance conclusions.

source_references.finding: PublicationDraft::encode freezes cursor/cut metadata, captures and fits the bounded checkpoint, serializes a structurally checked transition, and substitutes a bounded checkpoint transition when needed. These enforce replay/read-cut and wire-budget behavior; skipping the pipeline when no listener is currently attached changes late-reader semantics.

commit_display folds under the client lock, performs encode outside it, then installs the frozen publication before waking readers. The cost is present even in no-live-subscriber runs because the native projection remains maintained.

Live ReadDomainCut refresh reads a bounded transcript head, decorates response/process metadata, reads occupancy/projection head and trace total; read_live passes false so it already avoids trace-page materialization. The remaining 109/410 and 101/530 samples are not evidence of an omitted simple full-history scan removal.

persist_part captures field Facts, produces a sorted field index, and stores byte chunks for the exact retained Source. scalar at line 263 persists the frozen request detail Source. This supports bounded arbitrary-field navigation, exact byte slices and integrity checks, beyond storing a raw request JSON value.

FactSpool caps in-memory work at 256 facts/65536 bytes and spills into a SQLite temp table. INSERT, sorted SELECT and DELETE already use prepare_cached. Changing this representation or budget would require separate memory/correctness evidence, not a speculative final optimization.
from_validated_connection sets cache capacity 64 for both writer and reader connections. Connection::query_row/execute do not use that cache automatically.

NodeSqliteExecutor keeps a shared Map from SQL text to prepared StatementSync; run/get/all obtain statements through it (statement at line 111). Thus repeated fixed SQL avoids per-call prepare by construction. exec remains direct for SQL batches/transaction commands.

The SQLite storage path uses JSON.stringify through encodeJson for table writes (around 804-845) and document base/operation payloads (926). These inspected persistence paths do not construct rustX's validated per-field Source indexes or bounded native publication checkpoint/read-cut structures. This is a source-level explanation for residual different work, not a claim that all product features are equivalent or that such rustX features should be removed.

follow_up_decision.smallest_candidate: Use local prepare_cached for the two fixed SELECTs in observation_event::witness and the fixed-text completion_query SELECT in projection::completion_at. Keep SQL, parameters, sequence/cut bounds, optional/flatten behavior, decoding and errors unchanged. No new cache abstraction, lazy-validation bypass, increased cache capacity or SQL join is necessary.

sites.sql: SELECT observation_witness FROM events WHERE sequence=?1

SELECT COALESCE(r.direct=1 AND r.ready=1,0),e.observation_readiness_missing OR e.observation_unavailable FROM events e LEFT JOIN event_observation_readiness r ON r.sequence=e.sequence WHERE e.sequence=?1
completion_query(), constructed from a fixed COMPLETION_FIELDS constant; cache by its unchanged text

follow_up_decision.evidence: The union of sampled sqlite3LockAndPrepare stacks under witness or completion_at is 8/276 no-live-small, 6/284 no-live-large, 10/410 live-small, 18/530 live-large. Each sample is counted once in the union. This is an observed optimization opportunity, not a forecast that all these samples or this fraction of elapsed time would disappear.
follow_up_decision.broader_candidate: Live response reads still use direct fixed SELECTs in response_identity_source (sqlite.rs:2067), observation_members::transcript_process (observation_members.rs:363) and selected_layout/layout_at (observation_execution.rs:93/738). Their deduplicated prepare-stack union is 39/410 live-small and 26/530 live-large. A later focused caching pass could preserve all source-validity checks, but its wider SQL set should be tested and measured separately. Avoid collapsing repeated reads or removing validation merely because callers revisit the same cut.
follow_up_decision.recommendation: The three-query cache follow-up is justified if another full validation-and-measurement iteration is desired. It is not a correctness blocker and no benefit has been measured. Incorporating it into the final candidate requires source change, applicable Rust/integration checks, an O3 rebuild, and a complete fresh repeated unprofiled cohort (plus refreshed diagnostics if claiming final-profile coverage). If finishing this measured bundle, record it explicitly as a follow-up; do not imply it was implemented or measured.
